prompt: Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print style, Edo-period composition, flat perspective, bold contour lines, and minimal shading. A stylized interior classroom scene rendered as a traditional woodblock print. At the center-left, a student sits surrounded by many identical sheets arranged in repetitive patterns. The student is shown in a calm, focused posture, repeatedly writing the same solution across identical pages. The repetition is visually emphasized through patterned duplication rather than readable text. Behind the student, the background wall contains repeating abstract motifs symbolizing identical problems, using traditional wave-like or geometric ukiyo-e patterns instead of written content. On the right side, separated by empty space, the same student is depicted again facing a slightly different sheet. The posture is hesitant and uncertain, with a subtle shift in body language indicating confusion. Composition uses asymmetry: dense, patterned repetition on the left; open, sparse space on the right. Color palette: muted indigo blues, faded ochre, soft beige, and desaturated earth tones typical of Edo-period prints. Texture: visible woodblock grain, flat color fills, no gradients, no realistic lighting. Mood: quiet tension, subtle irony, imbalance between mastery and failure. No text, no readable symbols, no numbers, no modern elements, no photorealism.
tradition_approach: Used flat perspective, bold outlines, limited color palette, and repetitive patterns to reflect memorization while maintaining traditional ukiyo-e compositional asymmetry and texture.
